name: Coneflower (Echinacea)

schedule.notes: Cold-moist stratify 4 weeks in the fridge first — germination jumps from spotty to reliable.
Tolerates a light frost. Potted nursery plants establish faster than seed-grown.
First-year plants may bloom lightly; year 2+ blooms hard from midsummer to frost.

harvest.cues: Petals fully reflexed around a spiky bronze cone. Cut long stems for vases; goldfinches strip the seed heads in fall.
harvest.storageNotes: Cut flowers last 7 to 10 days in water. Leave some seed heads standing through winter for finches and structural interest.

varieties.name: Magnus
varieties.notes: Big horizontal petals (not drooping), deep rose-purple. Perennial Plant of the Year 1998.

varieties.name: White Swan
varieties.notes: Creamy white petals around an orange cone. Comes mostly true from seed.

varieties.name: Cheyenne Spirit
varieties.notes: Mix of red, orange, yellow, cream, pink. First-year flowering from seed.

notes: Tap-rooted — site it where you want it, mature plants resent moving. Leave seed heads standing for winter goldfinches and self-sown seedlings. Aster yellows (a phytoplasma) causes green deformed flowers; pull and burn affected plants, don't compost. Container-grown plants stay tidy and flower the same year.
